question: Should OpenClaw accept this disabled-by-default `agents.defaults.subagents` nudge/kill policy now, or should the linked stall-recovery issue stay open until maintainers decide default-on behavior, parent notification, and queue-level recovery semantics?
rationale: The implementation is plausible, but the linked issue is explicitly product-sensitive and the PR adds config plus automatic run-abort behavior that automation should not approve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Pause for design approval
options.body: Keep this PR open but require maintainer approval of default policy, notification semantics, and proof expectations before merge.

options.title: Accept opt-in scope
options.body: Treat disabled-by-default config as the first supported increment, leaving default-on and queue-level recovery for a follow-up issue.

options.title: Redirect to broader watchdog design
options.body: Close or supersede this PR if maintainers want stall recovery owned by the broader session activity watchdog instead of the subagent registry.

recommendation.title: Pause for design approval
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but require maintainer approval of default policy, notification semantics, and proof expectations before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits show broad ownership of subagent handoff, docs, and config surfaces touched by the policy decision.
